BoundNote.description: Content-free: the caller holds template.update, not note.read.
BoundNote.title: BoundNote

CalendarContextIn.description:
What the invite knew. ``description`` is read for its agenda and
then dropped — it is never stored and never returned.
CalendarContextIn.title: CalendarContextIn

ChoiceOption.description:
One selectable option of a ``choice``/``multi_choice`` section.

``value`` is the stable identity persisted in note content
(``field_specific_metadata``); renaming or removing a value is a
STRUCTURAL template edit because stored selections would dangle.
``voice_aliases`` fuel the sprint-13 extractor and are normalized
here (NFC, lower-case, stripped) so the extractor never
re-normalizes template data.
ChoiceOption.title: ChoiceOption

Constraints.description:
What a member's client needs to know — the effective rules, no
admin-only detail.
Constraints.title: Constraints

Coverage.description:
How the facts spread over the recording, and how much speech was
set aside. Counts and milliseconds only.
Coverage.title: Coverage

ExcludedRange.description:
A stretch of the recording left out of the notes, confirmed by code
(Summary Engine v2, Q2). ``reason`` is a closed vocabulary — background,
other_language, artifact, duplicate, unrelated — for the client to
turn into words; never text from the recording.
ExcludedRange.title: ExcludedRange

FieldType.description:
Sprint-06 shipped the first kinds; sprint-13 adds the two choice
kinds. Adding enum members is additive to the *model*; changing an
existing section's ``field_type`` remains a STRUCTURAL edit
(ADR-0016).
FieldType.title: FieldType

LinkView.description:
One share link. The token is returned only to people who may
manage the note (every route here checks that); it never appears in
audit or logs.
LinkView.title: LinkView

MeetingView.description:
What a second device needs to show the right status and to finish
the job the first one started.
MeetingView.title: MeetingView

NoteContent.description: The full content_jsonb body for one version.
NoteContent.title: NoteContent

SectionLabel.description:
Human-readable, localized title for one note section.

Templates are per-language (a template row is either ``uk`` or ``en``),
so the section ``name`` is a single string in the template's own
language. We mirror it into BOTH ``uk`` and ``en`` here — the same
behaviour the frontend's ``toStudioTemplate`` uses — so the SPA/PDF can
render section titles without re-fetching the template, and historical
notes carry their labels even if the template later changes.
SectionLabel.title: SectionLabel

SharedChanges.description:
What changed since this link last loaded the note (Sprint 23).
Keys only — the page highlights, it does not narrate.
SharedChanges.title: SharedChanges

TemplateDefinition.description:
Full template definition. Stored as ``templates.schema_jsonb``.

The top-level ``code`` + ``language`` pair is the human-readable
identifier; the row's UUID is the system identifier. Notes persist
the UUID + ``schema_version`` at finalization.
TemplateDefinition.title: TemplateDefinition

TemplateMetadata.description: Optional metadata attached to a template definition.
TemplateMetadata.title: TemplateMetadata

TemplateSection.description:
One section of a template. Each section is dictated separately
in sprint-06 section-aware mode.
TemplateSection.title: TemplateSection

WriterView.description:
Sprint L2 — who writes the notes on this deployment right now, and
whether that is the configured primary or its fallback.
WriterView.title: WriterView

put.description:
The whole policy, every time (the form sends what it shows). An
admin switching product mail back on clears the abuse guard's mark;
a free workspace may store `cta_enabled=false` but the page ignores
it (G-1).

post.description:
Tightening the policy revokes nothing by itself; this is the
explicit "and the links that already exist" — every live link in the
workspace, public and recipient, audited per note.

get.description: Every member may see who processes their meetings.

put.description:
Change the tier, the provider, the budget, or turn generation off.

Refuses with 409 and the exact list when the change would route to a
processor nobody has acknowledged. The list in the error is what the
client shows in the dialog — so what the admin reads and what the
router will do come from one place.

get.description:
Authenticated decrypt-and-stream (the DSAR download idiom): the
token narrows the window; it never replaces authentication.

post.description:
Put the workspace on the plan a code gives. Works with no payment
provider at all — that is what codes are for.

Add a calendar by its private iCal address — no Google client, no
OAuth. The feed is fetched once now so a wrong link fails here, not
silently on the home page.

schema.title: Response List Glossary V1 Glossary Get

post.description:
Remember one term.

Adding a term the workspace already has is not an error: it merges the
new mishearing into the existing entry and answers 200. Saying
"remember John Mayer" after two different mistakes should teach the
second one, not fail as a duplicate.

get.description:
The workspace's terms as the capture form's ``vocabulary_hint``.

The clients fetch this and pre-fill the field, so the transcriber has
the spellings before it guesses. It stays editable: the hint is a
suggestion about this meeting, not a setting.

delete.description:
Forget a term. Its creator, or an admin — a vocabulary one person
can quietly change for everyone is a vocabulary nobody trusts.

schema.title: Response Notes By Source Job V1 Notes By Source Job Get

post.description:
Open the note. Called as Record is pressed — the client must not
wait for it and must not let it stop the recording.

Idempotent on ``client_capture_id``: a retry, a double tap and a
second device that resumed the same capture all get the same note
(200 rather than 201).

schema.title: Expand

get.description:
The workspace's effective sharing rules, for any member's client
(Sprint 23).

delete.description:
Soft delete. The note leaves every list and read path and its
public links stop working; the row and its versions are kept.

503.description: Problem with `code` `model_not_configured` (no chat backend for this environment) or `model_unavailable` (the backend failed; `kind` names the failure class).

post.summary: Ask a question about this note (answered by the model over note + transcript).

get.description: What is still open from the previous meeting in this series.

post.description:
Tick a carried item off, re-open it, or drop it.

A tick by hand is `done_marked` and never `done_mentioned`: the
latter means the recording said so, with a quote, and only the
engine may claim that.

get.description:
Exactly what an external surface would render.

The preview and the shared page call the same pure builder, so "what
I saw in the preview" and "what the client got" cannot differ.

What is worth a second look before this goes to a client.

Warnings, not blockers. The author decides — a gate on sharing would
re-introduce exactly the lifecycle ADR-0051 removed.

422.description: Sprint-13 field-metadata validation failed: `field_metadata_invalid` (unknown keys / wrong shape / metadata on a field type that accepts none) or `choice_value_unknown` (a `selected` value not among the section's template options). Section-addressed problems in `problems[]`.

get.description:
Every verified fact behind this note, with the words that prove it.

Same audience as the transcript: these ARE transcript excerpts, so
the read goes through `require_view` and the oversight-read purpose
rule. The shared page never calls this.

schema.title: Response Generated Items V1 Notes  Note Id  Generated Items Get

post.description:
Write the note again from the recording.

Safe to press: the writer rewrites only sections nobody has edited
since the last run, so the author's own text survives a regenerate
exactly as it survives the first pass.

schema.title: Response List Items V1 Notes  Note Id  Items Get

patch.description:
Fix a line's owner or its date, in place.

The body is not touched, so the key does not change and everything
attached to it survives: the recipient's confirmation on the shared
page, this note's correction history, and the evidence chip once there
is one. That is the whole reason this route exists rather than telling
the author to edit the text.

Addressed under ``/items/by-key/`` because ``PATCH /items/{item_id}``
was already taken by the Sprint 20 status route, which addresses items
by their row UUID.

post.description:
Take a line out of the note, and say why.

The reason is the valuable part: it is a closed vocabulary, it carries
no text, and it is what tells us next week which kinds of line we
should stop writing. Idempotent — dismissing a line that is already
gone answers 200 rather than 404, because the author's intent has been
honoured either way.

Put a dismissed line back, exactly as it read.

The text comes from the version history rather than from a column: the
correction log holds no note text on purpose, and the hash chain
already has every word. The line returns to the bottom of the section
it came from — guessing its old position would be a second edit the
author did not ask for.

schema.title: Response List Links V1 Notes  Note Id  Links Get

post.description:
Mint a link for one recipient. Idempotent per e-mail address: a
second call for the same address answers 200 with the existing link
rather than minting one the sheet cannot tell apart.

200.description: A live link for that recipient e-mail already exists.

post.description:
The recording reached asr-service: bind the job to the note.

Idempotent for the same pair. A job another note already owns is a
409 ``already_assigned`` — the partial unique index on
``notes.source_asr_job_id`` is the single source of that truth,
shared with ``from-transcript``.

The recording was discarded or never happened. The note stays — it
holds what the author typed, which is the part that cannot be redone.

"This continues…" — link this meeting to an earlier one by hand.

Restricted to notes this author may view, like every other path into
another note's content.

put.description:
When each typed line was first touched, relative to the recording.

First report wins: the line was typed once, and a later flush of the
same key is the same line being edited, not heard again.

Idempotent: a note has at most one live link, and asking again
returns it rather than minting a second.

post.description:
The author clears a response (a resolved dispute, an abusive
comment). The row stays, stamped with who cleared it and when.

schema.title: Response List Section Audio Segments V1 Notes  Note Id  Sections  Section Key  Audio Clips Get

post.description:
Mail the note to the people the sharer named, from the server.

Two kinds of recipient, one button. A workspace member is granted
access and mailed a link to the note in the app; anybody else gets
their own recipient link (minted here, one per address, reused when
it already exists) so the sender can see who opened it and turn one
off without the others. The mail says plainly that anyone holding
the link can read it.

Sending is per-recipient and never raises: one dead address must not
swallow the four mails that would have arrived. The response says
what happened to each one so the sender can fix a typo rather than
wonder.

The transcription finished: put it in the note.

Called by ANY client of the author, on any device — which is how a
meeting survives the laptop being closed mid-transcription. The job's
ownership is proven the only way that is safe: by fetching the result
with the caller's own bearer, so asr-service applies its own tenant
and permission checks.

schema.title: Response List Versions V1 Notes  Note Id  Versions Get

get.description:
Opt out of recipient mail from EVERY workspace, in one click, with
no login and no address in the URL. The page is the same whether the
signature verified or not: a forged link learns nothing, and a real
one is honoured silently.

Count the click server-side (so it counts without JavaScript) and
send the browser to the web app's lead page. The only destination is
``MDX_APP_BASE_URL`` + a fixed path — nothing from the request decides
where the redirect goes.

The sender workspace's logo. Public to anyone holding a token —
that is the sender's choice when they upload one (validated to an
image type and 2 MB at upload).

post.description:
A recipient says something is wrong with this page. Stored,
audited, the workspace's admins told; three `spam` reports against
one sender's links switch that workspace's product mail off until an
admin turns it back on.

Spend the code. Five wrong answers retire it; success is remembered
on the link (whoever controls the mailbox is the recipient), and the
page comes back with `can_respond` on.

Mail a six-digit code to the address the link was sent to. 202
whatever happens: a link with no address, or one that is already
verified, learns nothing from the answer.
